assignment.acceptance_condition: Stated and proved theorems: an explicit upper bound N(H) <= f(H) with constants, the proof of the per-edge growth factor and branching bounds it rests on, and a rigorous two-sided depth-log H relation; any sharper-but-unproved improvement must be labeled as conjecture with supporting reasoning kept separate from the proved bound.
assignment.objective: From first principles, prove the strongest rigorous upper bound attainable for N(H), the number of sorted solutions with maximum coordinate at most H, and analyze rigorously how mutation depth (distance from the root (1,1,1,1), well-defined once the tree structure holds) relates to log H. Expected components, to be proved or improved: (i) every child of a non-root vertex has maximum at least 3 times the parent's maximum (since mutating at any coordinate below the maximum d gives a new value >= (4ab-1)d with ab >= 1), hence depth(v) <= log_3(max(v)) and max(v) >= 3^{depth(v)}; (ii) every non-root vertex has at most 3 children and the root has exactly 1, giving a crude N(H) = O(H); (iii) sharpen the O(H) bound as far as rigorously possible (e.g., by analyzing coincidences between children, forced sorting effects, or refined growth factors larger than 3 on most branches), and give a two-sided relation between depth and log H along extremal branches (fastest- and slowest-growing chains). No growth law may be assumed; every bound must come with explicit constants and complete proofs.
assignment.rationale: D4 (upper side) and D6 (depth vs log H) share the same engine - the multiplicative growth of the maximum along tree edges - so coupling them avoids duplicate lemma work and yields the strongest combined statement.

context.product_intent: This run tests mathematical discovery and proof, not research composition: the memorandum exists to establish from first principles, with complete proofs, what is true about the Markov-Hurwitz n=4 mutation graph and the growth of solution counts N(H), with theorems cleanly separated from labeled, reproducible observations and from conjecture. Honest partial progress with clearly stated obstructions — and no assumed growth law — is the explicit acceptance standard, so the product's value lies in rigor and in identifying the most informative next mathematical step.
stable_context: SC1: S is the set of sorted positive-integer quadruples (a,b,c,d), 1 <= a <= b <= c <= d, satisfying a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2 = 4abcd (raw request).
SC2: A Vieta mutation replaces one coordinate x_i by 4 times the product of the other three coordinates minus x_i, followed by sorting; permutations are identified (raw request).
SC3: The request designates (1,1,1,1) as the root; substitution gives 4 = 4, so it lies in S.
SC4: N(H) denotes the number of sorted solutions with maximum coordinate at most H (raw request).

SC5: Directly from SC1-SC2: mutating (1,1,1,1) at any coordinate gives 3, and (1,1,1,3) satisfies the equation (1+1+1+9 = 12 = 4*3), so the root has at least one neighbor; such immediate arithmetic may seed sanity checks but must be labeled as observation in the memo (inferred from stated definitions).

context.task: Investigate the mutation graph of sorted positive-integer solutions of a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2 = 4abcd under Vieta mutation. First prove or refute the structural claims — connectivity of every solution to (1,1,1,1), uniqueness of a height-decreasing mutation at every non-root vertex, and the consequent rooted-tree structure of the quotient graph — then pursue the open asymptotic part: strongest attainable rigorous upper and lower bounds for N(H), the relation between mutation depth and log H, an active search for exceptional small solutions, hidden cycles, multiple parents, and induction failure modes, and sharply separated conjectures. Deliver a self-contained research memorandum.
